mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW 4 Series 420d engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A replacement engine for a BMW 420d typically costs between £1,800 and £6,500 depending on condition. Used N47D20C units start from around £1,800, while reconditioned units range from £2,800 to £5,500. Rebuilt engines with warranty sit at £3,800-£6,500. Specialist fitting adds approximately £650-£910 in labour.

mainEntity.name: Which BMW 4 Series 420d engines have timing chain problems?

acceptedAnswer.text: The N47D20C engine fitted to 420d models from 2013-2015 has a well-documented timing chain weakness. The rear-mounted chain can stretch over time, particularly with extended oil service intervals. The later B47D20A engine (2015 onwards) addressed this issue with a revised front-chain design and is significantly more reliable.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a BMW 4 Series 420d?

acceptedAnswer.text: A 2013-2015 420d is typically worth £3,780-£12,600. If your car is worth under £5,000, a used engine replacement is usually the most cost-effective route. For cars worth over £8,000, a reconditioned or rebuilt engine with warranty is a sound investment - especially if you plan to keep the car for 2+ years.

mainEntity.name: How long does a BMW 4 Series 420d engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: Supply-only engines are typically dispatched within 1-2 working days. Full supply & fit through a specialist workshop usually takes 2-3 days, depending on workshop availability and the complexity of the specific 420d variant (xDrive models may take slightly longer).

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the BMW 420d and 425d engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 420d uses a 2.0-litre four-cylinder diesel producing 184-190hp. The 425d uses the same 2.0-litre B47D20B engine but with a twin-turbo setup producing 224hp. While both are 2.0-litre diesels, the 425d's additional turbo and higher output mean different engine codes and compatibility.

mainEntity.name: Can I replace my N47 engine with a B47 in my BMW 420d?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes - the B47D20A is a direct replacement for the N47D20C in the 420d, as both engines share the same mounting points and transmission compatibility. Upgrading to a B47 offers improved reliability (revised timing chain design) and Euro 6 emissions compliance. Always verify compatibility via VIN check before ordering.

historyTimeline.h2: BMW 4 Series 420d - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The BMW 420d joined the 4 Series range at launch in 2013 as the entry-level diesel, offering a compelling blend of economy and performance. Over its production run, the 420d underwent a crucial engine change from the N47 to the more robust B47, addressing reliability concerns and meeting tightening emissions standards.

milestones.description: N47D20C, 2.0-litre turbo-diesel, 184hp - original 420d engine for F32/F33/F36 chassis
B47D20A, 2.0-litre turbo-diesel, 190hp - Euro 6-compliant successor to the N47, introduced as part of the Life Cycle Impulse (LCI) for the 4 Series range
420d receives 48V mild-hybrid technology as part of the G22 generation launch, improving efficiency and low-end response

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the BMW 4 Series 420d is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: BMW 4 Series 420d Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The BMW 420d is powered by either the N47D20C (2013-2015) or the B47D20A (2015-present). While the B47 is significantly more reliable, N47-equipped 420ds have a well-documented timing chain weakness that drives most replacement decisions. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure point, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Failure - Why the BMW 4 Series 420d N47 Engine Wears Prematurely
problems.rootCause: The N47's rear-mounted timing chain design uses components that stretch over time, particularly where oil service intervals have been extended. A rattling noise from the rear of the engine on cold start is the primary warning sign.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Chain kit replacement only, no engine removal required on some variants
repairOptions.longevity: Best if caught early (cold-start rattle only, no misfires)

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty【EM-QUOTE】
repairOptions.longevity: When chain has snapped or engine is otherwise damaged

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2013-2015 BMW 420d is worth approximately £3,780-£12,600 depending on mileage and condition. For sub-£5,000 examples, a used engine replacement typically makes more sense than a full rebuilt unit. For cars worth £8,000+, a reconditioned or rebuilt engine usually justifies the premium via warranty and reliability.
problems.recommendation: If you hear the tell-tale cold-start rattle and act quickly, a timing chain replacement (preventative) is the most cost-effective option. If the chain has already snapped or engine damage is extensive, replacement with a rebuilt B47D20A unit (with its improved chain design) is the smarter long-term play.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt N47D20C BMW 4 Series 420d engine prices

problems.h4: EGR Cooler Failure - BMW 4 Series 420d B47 Engine
problems.rootCause: The EGR cooler can develop internal leaks, allowing coolant to enter the exhaust system. BMW issued a recall for this issue.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement EGR cooler, coolant flush, system bleed
repairOptions.longevity: If caught early - warning light or coolant loss
If EGR failure has caused secondary damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: For a 2015-2018 BMW 420d valued at £8,000-£18,000, the EGR repair is well within the vehicle's value. Replacement is only justified if the engine has suffered consequential damage.
problems.recommendation: Address EGR cooler issues promptly - the repair is relatively straightforward and far cheaper than a full engine replacement. Always check if your car is covered by the BMW recall.
